newsitem.title: FRANCE: French stockmarket falls sharply in early trade.
newsitem.headline: French stockmarket falls sharply in early trade.

text.p: French stocks opened sharply lower on Friday as the bourse tracked sharp falls in U.S., Asian and other European stockmarkets.
The blue chip CAC-40 index was down 26.79 points or 1.2 percent lower at 2,185.32 at 1000 GMT after steadying from an early slide that took it as low as 2,171.57.
The CAC-40 December futures contract was down 27 points at 2,188 -- a major support level that appeared to be holding.
Trading began on a bad note as investors around the world were selling equities, beginning with a near-100-point plunge in the Dow Jones industrial average on Thursday.
"People are getting more and more nervous about Wall Street," said Olivier Blitz, chief salesman at brokerage IFF.
He said he was still optimistic about the French market's prospects for 1997 "but I think the current consolidation isn't finished".
The CAC index has shed 180 points since December 3 when it came within striking distance of its all-time record of 2,360.98 points set in February 1994.
Traders said President Jacques Chirac's television appearance on Thursday night did not reassure people. "He's holding the line and it may be the wrong line," one trader said.
Chirac said he was not going back on pledges to cut unemployment, but reiterated that France must first put its finances in order.
He also said it would be wrong to devalue the franc. Many bourse investors worry the 'strong franc' policy is holding back the French economy.
All 40 CAC components were lower on Friday, with building group Bouygues registering the biggest loss of 3.1 percent.
Bouygues said on Thursday that it planned to buy glass-maker Saint-Gobain's Cise unit for 2.16 billion francs if a proposed merger of the companies' Cise and Saur units succeeded.
